input: Support engineers handle live chat, but several of them type slowly and cannot keep up with three concurrent conversations, even with every tool and permission they need.
notes: bodily skill (typing speed), environment already provided

input: On-call engineers are supposed to write a detailed handover after the night shift, but after 12 hours awake they are too physically exhausted to do it properly, although the template is short and they know how.
New hires don't add feature flags because nobody told them flags are expected for risky changes, and they don't know the SDK call.
People agree the rollback checklist matters but keep forgetting the third step, which is a rarely used CLI flag.
Everyone agrees the pre-push test run is valuable, but it takes 11 minutes, so engineers skip it to stay in flow.
notes: time friction; agreeing but not acting is not reflective-motivation

input: The postmortem template lives in a wiki page three clicks deep, and nothing reminds the incident lead when an incident closes.
Juniors don't ask questions in the support channel because no senior engineer ever posts there and asking feels like admitting ignorance.
The team norm is to approve PRs without comments; the one reviewer who leaves detailed feedback gets teased for slowing things down.
Engineers have access, know how, and have time to write contract tests, but they believe the tests never catch real bugs and are a waste of effort.
Product engineers skip accessibility checks because their quarterly goals reward shipping velocity only, and the checks count against it.
Engineers agree with the alert runbook and find it fast to follow, but alert noise has trained them to swipe away pages on reflex.
The weekly ticket-grooming takes two minutes and everyone supports it, yet people dread it because it feels tedious and push it off out of habit.
Engineers want to check the service dashboard during incidents, but most of them were never granted access to the observability org.
notes: access is opportunity in COM-B (Michie 2011), not capability
